headline: THE OFFER ON 198 RENA HAS BEEN SITTING WITH YOUR OWN SELLERS FOR TWELVE HOURS WITH NO REPLY — the breakdown, both net sheets and your recommended counter went to them at 5:38 this morning and nothing has come back, which means the counter never reached the buyer's side today at all; meanwhile the money fuse The Daily set for 10:00 AM burned all the way through the day unanswered and the scheduled draft clears in the morning. · DO: call SBA + PNC before that draft clears · WATCH: 198 Rena sellers silent 12h on the counter package (8/4) · ✅ CLOSED TODAY: the Lake Crest 8/20 date question you chased for 30 hours was answered at 4:12 this afternoon.

notes: ✅ HALF THE PUBLISHING BLOCK IS FIXED AS OF THIS RUN. The GitHub Pages repo that serves both phone boards had never been cloned to the MacBook — it has been cloned back this evening to the exact path the routine expects, and both rebuilt JSONs are staged in it. ⚠️ ONE STEP IS LEFT AND IT NEEDS YOU: the GitHub CLI is still signed out, so the push could not run. Sign in once (`gh auth login`) and every future run publishes on its own. Until then what you are reading on your phone is this morning's 8:05 build.

⛔ SHOWING BOARD OUTREACH REMAINS SUSPENDED — your own ruling, option (c). The two send-safety ledgers that record which buyer's agents have already been emailed did not survive the migration and are genuinely absent from Drive. So the Showing Board keeps building normally and every hot signal becomes a call task for you instead of a machine email. Zero duplicate-email risk, and no invented ledger was created to fake one.

⚠️ TWO WORKER ROUTINES RAN HALF-BLIND TODAY, BOTH FOR MISSING-DATA REASONS, NEITHER SILENT: the Brivity deep sweep hit a dead single-sign-on wall at 5:45 PM and imported nothing (it is costing roughly twenty likely-to-sell records a day and there is already a p2 to re-authorise it), and the marketing engagement run could not see its listing coverage files because that folder has not been migrated yet. Separately the draft counter on this page is carried from the 1:42 PM verified count — the mail connector's draft listing is returning one draft when at least seven exist, so treat that number as last-known rather than live.

callBlock.who: Mallory W. — the co-op agent holding the only buyer on this board who has said the words "wants to put an offer in"
callBlock.why: 🔥 STILL THE BEST BUYER SIGNAL YOU HAVE, AND IT IS NOW TWO FULL DAYS OLD. She toured the Altamont unit Monday at 1:00, phoned at 1:43 to say her client "really, really liked it" and wants to write but needs to save a little more for the down payment, and asked to be kept in the loop if another offer lands. Her written form agreed in every field: interested YES, priced JUST RIGHT. ⭐ THE OBSTACLE IS FINANCING TIMING, NOT PRICE OR CONDITION — which is the solvable kind. ⚠️ You emailed her Monday at 5:00 and the follow-up has been staged as an unsent draft since 5:51 yesterday morning. Thirty-six hours of a machine holding a conversation open. ⭐ THREE QUESTIONS CONVERT THIS AND THEY ONLY WORK ON THE PHONE: how far out is she really, has she actually spoken to a lender, and would seller-paid closing costs or a longer close bridge the gap.

callBlock.who: Kim W. — she asked you to call twice inside twenty-five seconds, then asked again at lunch
callBlock.why: 🔥 THE MOST DIRECT ASK ON YOUR BOARD AND IT HAS NOW BEEN OPEN ALL DAY. Two "call me" messages landed twenty-five seconds apart this morning, and at 1:21 this afternoon she came back with a specific, concrete request — she needs a resource for a slab leak. ⭐ THAT SECOND MESSAGE IS THE GIFT: it turns an unexplained callback into a five-minute call where you already know the answer she wants. ⚠️ A client who has to ask three times stops asking. This is the cheapest relationship save on the list.

callBlock.who: Cynthia W. — new buyer off the Fieldstone ad, and the phone is the only channel that exists
callBlock.why: 🔥 HER EMAIL HARD BOUNCED, WHICH MEANS EVERY AUTOMATED LANE THIS SYSTEM HAS IS ALREADY DEAD ON HER. No D0, no D2, no drip — nothing the machine sends will ever arrive. ⭐ SHE IS ONE OF SIX NAMED BUYERS THAT A SINGLE LISTING AD PRODUCED IN FOUR DAYS, which is the best lead-source signal on the board right now and worth protecting. ⛔ If you do not dial this one personally, nobody does. There is no fallback lane behind you.

callBlock.who: Anthony M. — third name off the same Fieldstone ad, re-engaged Sunday, and has NEVER been touched
callBlock.why: 🔴 ZERO TOUCHES EVER, ON A LEAD THAT CAME BACK ON ITS OWN. He re-engaged at 4:30 Sunday afternoon without any prompting from us, which is the strongest passive buying signal a database record can produce — and the file shows not one outbound attempt against him since. ⭐ THE AD THAT MADE HIM HAS NOW PRODUCED SIX NAMED BUYERS IN FOUR DAYS. Speed-to-lead is the only thing that converts this class, and the clock on him is measured in days now, not hours.

callBlock.who: Lisa S. — fourth Fieldstone-ad buyer, landed Sunday evening while the responder was still down
callBlock.why: ⚠️ SHE ARRIVED AT 7:47 SUNDAY NIGHT INSIDE THE OUTAGE WINDOW, so the instant responder never fired on her and she has had no first touch at all. That is a machine failure, not a lead-quality problem — she did everything right and got silence. ⭐ The responder is verified alive again and fired correctly four separate times today, so the lane behind her is healthy; she is simply the one who fell through the hole. Treat this as a recovery call, not a cold call.

callBlock.who: David C. — the first name off the Fieldstone ad, and your own email promised him a call
callBlock.why: 🔴 THE OLDEST BROKEN PROMISE ON THIS LIST, DUE SINCE 7/31. The first-touch email that went to him states, in writing, that you would call him that day. Four days later that has not happened. ⚠️ THIS IS THE ONE WITH ACTUAL DOWNSIDE — the others are simply un-worked; this one has a written commitment against it that the client can read. ⭐ The fix is one dial and an honest opener; the cost of not making it is a lead who watched us say we would call and then not call.

callBlock.who: Nolan H. — he answered a text in two minutes with "I don't know yet"
callBlock.why: ⭐ A TWO-MINUTE REPLY IS NOT A NO — IT IS THE FASTEST RESPONSE ON YOUR ENTIRE BOARD. Nobody who is genuinely uninterested answers that quickly. "I don't know yet" is a timing answer, not a rejection, and it is exactly the shape of lead that a single conversation either qualifies or retires cleanly. ⭐ Either outcome is worth more than leaving it in the maybe pile: he either has a real window you can plan around, or he comes off the p1 list and stops costing you attention every morning.

callBlock.who: The DNC rule — a decision, not a call, and it is currently blocking six of your own inbound leads
callBlock.why: 🔴 SIX PEOPLE TYPED THEIR NUMBER INTO YOUR OWN IDX FORM AND THE SYSTEM WILL NOT TEXT THEM, because those numbers carry a do-not-call marker from a source outside your site. ⭐ THE TENSION IS REAL AND IT IS YOURS TO RULE ON: they asked us to contact them on that number, and the marker says a different list said otherwise. ⚠️ Until you rule, the machine's default is silence — which is the safest legal answer and the worst business one, and it is quietly costing you six inbound leads that raised their own hands.

listings.status: 🔴 Active $450K — the offer is real and formal, and your sellers have now been silent on it for twelve hours
listings.note: 🔴 THE SILENCE IS THE STORY TONIGHT, NOT THE OFFER. At 5:38 this morning both sellers received one email carrying the terms, what the buyers want to keep, both net sheets and your recommended counter — opening "We have a written offer on 198 Rena — and after 75 days on market, that's good news." ⚠️ TWELVE HOURS LATER NOTHING HAS COME BACK, which means the counter has not gone to the buyer's side at any point today. The paper is sitting still on your own side of the table. ⭐ THAT IS WORTH A PHONE CALL TONIGHT, NOT ANOTHER EMAIL — a two-seller decision on a first offer after 75 days is exactly the kind that stalls out of uncertainty rather than disagreement, and a five-minute call usually unsticks it. ⭐ THE LEVERAGE, IF THE OFFER IS LIGHT, IS EVIDENCE AND NOT OPINION: two independent agents toured this house across 75 days and NEITHER ONE TOUCHED THE PRICE QUESTION — every price and price-recommendation field on both forms came back blank. The stated objections were the upstairs bathroom (7/31: "deal breaker because of the kids") and a compartmentalized interior (7/12: "She LOVED the yard and lot"). Nobody who walked it said the number was wrong; they said the floor plan wasn't theirs. 38 buyers have it saved against 715 views. ⛔ THE OFFER TERMS ARE DELIBERATELY WITHHELD FROM THIS PAGE — it is public and live negotiation numbers do not belong on it. ⚠️ Quote $450,000 only.

listings.status: ✅ Under contract $899K — the 30-hour date question closed at 4:12 this afternoon, and the inspection column is finished
listings.note: ✅ THIS ONE CAME OFF THE WATCH LIST TODAY. The buyer's agent asked Monday at 10:14 to move closing to August 20 at 3:00; you answered "OK, will talk w seller" five minutes later, and for thirty hours this panel carried it as the board's oldest unkept promise. ⭐ IT CLOSED AT 4:12 THIS AFTERNOON via the office relay — the loop is shut and the item is retired. ⭐ AND YOUR SIDE HAS NO RISK LEFT IN THE DECISION: the appraisal came back complete and clean Monday afternoon, and this morning's 11:00 septic was the last inspection item on the file. With the inspection column effectively finished, a date move costs you nothing operationally. ⛔ SIX DAYS OF SLIP IS STILL AN ASK, NOT AN AGREED DATE — 8/14 remains the receipted close date until something executed says otherwise, and the reason for the slip is their buyer's own sale, not anything on your side. Say that out loud when the date gets papered. ⚠️ Also live on this client: a family member ran a CMA that the office transferred to you at 12:04 today — raise it on the same call rather than starting a separate thread.

listings.status: 🔥 Active — the price came down today and a new showing booked within hours of it
listings.note: 🔥 THE PRICE MOVED TODAY AND THE MARKET ANSWERED THE SAME AFTERNOON. The MLS line on this listing read $299,000 as recently as last night's seller report; today's 1:50 PM showing notice reads $295,000 · ACTIVE against the same MLS ID. ⚠️ ONE SYSTEM RECEIPT, SO TREAT THE EXACT FIGURE AS THE MLS FIELD RATHER THAN A CONFIRMED STRATEGY — but the field itself changed between two machine reads twenty hours apart, which is as close to a receipt as a price cut produces. ⭐ AND THEN A NEW SHOWING BOOKED FOR THURSDAY 8/6 AT 11:00 AM — the first fresh booking this listing has taken since the cut appeared. Sequence, not proven causation, but it is the sequence you wanted. ⭐ THE CASE FOR MOVING WAS ALREADY BUILT AND IT WAS THREE READS DEEP: Sunday's buyer filed interested YES with "too high" attached in the same form, staged 4 of 5 — the highest this listing has recorded — and named a competing house she is weighing it against. Two earlier reads pointed the same way. ⛔ NOBODY HAS EVER NAMED A REPLACEMENT NUMBER — every price-recommendation field on all three came back blank, so do not let anyone infer one from this page. ✅ The outreach to that buyer's agent went out yesterday evening in your own voice and is still unanswered; the competing house she named is the clock.

listings.status: ⚠️ Active $559K — the first read since the contract died came back today, and it is a price objection
listings.note: ⚠️ THE FIRST FEEDBACK THIS LISTING HAS RETURNED SINCE THE CONTRACT FELL THROUGH ON 7/27 LANDED AT 2:08 THIS AFTERNOON, and it is the one answer this file did not want. Off the 11:45 AM tour: interested — NO. Priced right — TOO HIGH. Staging — 2 of 5, the lowest score this listing has ever recorded. Price-change recommendation — BLANK. No comment left. ⭐ WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ONE FORM NORMALLY WOULD: the two reads immediately before the contract both said JUST RIGHT while objecting to other things. This is the first "too high" since the deal died, and it arrives on the first tour after the house went back on market — the exact read a re-listed property is graded on. ⛔ IT IS STILL ONE OPINION AND THE PRICE FIELD WAS BLANK — nobody has named a number, and one form is not a pricing decision. ⭐ BUT THE STAGING 2 IS ACTIONABLE TONIGHT AND COSTS NOTHING: the earlier reads on this house scored staging 3 and 4 and flagged it as dirty with glitching electrical. A 2 on the same house after a fall-through says presentation has decayed while it sat, and that is fixable without touching the price. ⭐ This is an institutional seller — give them the read straight, with the staging number next to the price answer, and let them decide.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $380K — the sixth tour in seven days ran at 11:00 today, and the competing-offer question is still open
listings.note: 🔥 SIX TOURS IN SEVEN DAYS, FIVE DIFFERENT BROKERAGES, ON A HOUSE THAT TOOK EXACTLY ONE SHOWING IN ITS FIRST ELEVEN DAYS. Today's ran at 11:00 after sliding twice — 9:00 to 10:00 to 11:00 — which is the third clear-out these owner-occupants have absorbed in twenty-four hours. ⭐ THEY DESERVE TO HEAR THE PATTERN, NOT JUST THE APPOINTMENTS: the traffic is real and it is accelerating, and that is worth saying to people who keep leaving their own house. ⚠️ NO WRITTEN READ HAS RETURNED FROM TODAY'S TOUR YET. ⭐ THE LIVE THREAD IS STILL MONDAY'S 6:15 PM SHOWING AND IT IS THE HOTTEST THING ON THIS FILE: the sellers' own doorbell camera caught it — Dennis wrote at 8:48 that night, "the mom said she loved it multiple times, talked about how much they liked the grass." 🔥 AND THEN THE BUYER SIDE CALLED TO ASK ABOUT COMPETITION at 8:30 that evening — an assistant asking whether there are any offers in or expected. ⭐ THAT QUESTION IS THE SIGNAL. Agents do not ask about competing offers on houses their buyers are lukewarm on. It has still not been answered, and answering it honestly — in either direction — is the move that either produces paper or clears the deck. ⭐ The ad driving all of it has now produced six named buyers in four days.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $164K — a named buyer wants to write, and the follow-up to her agent is a 36-hour-old unsent draft
listings.note: 🔥 THE ONLY UNQUALIFIED YES ON THE WHOLE BOARD IS ON THIS $164,000 UNIT. Monday's 1:00 PM tour produced the first YES this listing has ever recorded: interested YES, priced JUST RIGHT, and verbatim — "Client loves the space and the fact that it has room for washer and dryer." Her agent phoned three minutes before the form landed to say the client "really, really liked it" and "wants to put an offer in" but needs to save a little more for the down payment, and asked to be told if any other offer arrives. ⭐ THAT LAST REQUEST IS THE TELL — people who ask to be warned about competition are planning to compete. ⚠️ THE BLOCKER IS FINANCING TIMING AND NOTHING ELSE. She wrote JUST RIGHT on the price. Do not read this as a pricing signal. ⚠️ AND THE FOLLOW-UP HAS BEEN AN UNSENT DRAFT SINCE 5:51 YESTERDAY MORNING — thirty-six hours of a machine holding open a conversation a phone call would close. This is the single clearest case on the board for the rule that a staged draft is not follow-up. ⭐ A second buyer walked it Saturday and has gone three days silent; a July tour noted puddling in the little patio area and is still deciding.

listings.status: ✅ Under contract $369K — inspection TOMORROW, close receipted 8/31, and nothing is owed by your side
listings.note: ✅ THE CLEANEST FILE ON THE BOARD AND IT SHOULD STAY THAT WAY. Home inspection runs tomorrow, Wednesday 8/5; the close date is receipted at 8/31; the contract-to-close packet went out Monday at 12:09 and title confirmed receipt at 12:57. ⭐ TWO PIECES OF PAPERWORK LANDED THIS AFTERNOON AND NEITHER ONE TOUCHES YOUR SELLERS' NET — which is the useful thing to know before either of them calls you about it. The dotloop addendum that arrived at 3:15 is an ADDRESS CORRECTION: the title file has been running "Lake View Dr" against a property on Lake View Cir, and fixing it now is exactly right. ⭐ AND THE CLIENT-CARE FEE DISCLOSED AT 3:42 IS PAYABLE BY THE BUYER, not your sellers — worth having that answer ready rather than looking it up on the call. ⚠️ The inspection itself is still ahead, so the milestone stays at INSPECTION and the file is not clear yet; a co-op fee of 2.5% seller-paid is receipted on the closing sheet.

listings.status: ⚠️ Active $1.15M — Sunday's open house is three days back and still nothing has captured it
listings.note: ⚠️ THE BIGGEST LISTING ON YOUR BOARD HELD AN OPEN HOUSE ON SUNDAY AND THIS DESK STILL CANNOT SEE WHAT HAPPENED AT IT — no traffic count, no sign-in sheet, no debrief, three days on. ⭐ THAT IS NOT A CRITICISM OF THE EVENT, IT IS A GAP IN THE RECORD: on a $1,150,000 listing the open-house debrief is the single highest-value piece of intelligence the week produces, and right now it exists only in your head. Five minutes of dictation makes it usable by every other routine. ⭐ THE ONE WRITTEN READ THIS FILE HAS IS AN ACREAGE OBJECTION, NOT A PRICE ONE: off the 7/29 tour, verbatim — "He likes the house but the land isn't what he is looking for." ⭐ AND THE LAND COMPONENT WAS CLARIFIED TODAY: the office confirmed at 2:45 that the parcel runs 40 acres. On a file where the stated objection is the land, knowing exactly what the land is changes how the next conversation goes. ✅ The sellers on this file are verified.

listings.client: Six named buyers in four days

listings.note: 🔥 ONE LISTING AD HAS PRODUCED SIX NAMED BUYER LEADS IN FOUR DAYS, which makes it the highest-yielding marketing asset on the board by a wide margin. ⚠️ AND THE CONVERSION SIDE IS WHERE IT IS LEAKING: four of the six are sitting on your call list right now with zero completed contact, one of them since 7/31 against an email that promised him a call that day, and one of them reachable only by phone because her email hard bounced. ⭐ THE LESSON IS NOT "RUN MORE ADS" — IT IS THAT THE ADS ARE ALREADY WORKING AND THE PHONE IS THE BOTTLENECK. Six leads in four days is a genuine win; six leads in four days with four uncalled is a slow leak in the best thing you have running. ⭐ An hour of dialing tonight clears the entire backlog this source has created.

listings.status: 🔴 Active $189K — the cut was approved eleven days ago and is still unverified, twenty-one days without a showing
listings.note: 🔴 THE LONGEST-RUNNING UNFINISHED ITEM ON THE BOARD. A price cut was approved on this listing eleven days ago and there is still no receipt anywhere that it actually took effect in the MLS. ⚠️ WHICH MEANS THE RISK IS TWO PUBLIC PRICES, NOT A SLOW SALE — a stale number in one syndication feed against a corrected one in another is a real problem on a listing whose only written read said the price was too high. ⭐ TWENTY-ONE DAYS WITHOUT A SINGLE SHOWING, on the same client whose other two listings are producing live buyers. That contrast is the argument for whatever the next move is. ⭐ The only feedback on file is from 7/23: not interested, price TOO HIGH, rating 3 of 5. ✅ The verification takes two minutes and closes an eleven-day-old loop — pull the MLS line and confirm the number that is actually public.

listings.note: 🔴 DAY FIVE OF A SELLER NOT HEARING GOOD NEWS. The 7/31 read on this unit came back with all five answers filled in and the useful one is this: the buyer's opinion of the price was JUST RIGHT, with an overall rating of 4 of 5. The client answer was "not interested," but the price was explicitly validated by somebody with no reason to flatter it. ⭐ THAT IS EXACTLY THE FEEDBACK A SELLER SITTING ON A BEACH CONDO WANTS TO HEAR, and it has been sitting in this system unshared since Friday. ⚠️ A validated price plus no buyer is a marketing conversation, not a pricing one — and you cannot have that conversation with someone who does not know the price was validated. ⭐ An eleven-day-old gap also sits on this file: a 7/25 tour left a note in the app and the nudge has never been answered, so there is written material there to go get.

listings.status: 🔴 Active — she called Friday and the tenant answer is now eleven days owed
listings.note: 🔴 ELEVEN DAYS ON A QUESTION A CLIENT ASKED DIRECTLY. She called Friday to follow up on a tenant question that has been outstanding since late July. ⚠️ THE PROBLEM IS NOT THE ANSWER, IT IS THE FOLLOWING UP TO GET IT — a client who has to chase twice for something this ordinary starts assuming the harder questions will go the same way. ⭐ THIS IS A SIXTY-SECOND CALL WHETHER OR NOT YOU HAVE THE ANSWER: "here is where it stands and here is when you will have it" costs nothing and resets the clock honestly. Silence is the only version of this that damages anything. ⚠️ No showings recorded on this listing in the window.

Worth thirty seconds to confirm nothing else is sitting in the same blind spot. ⛔ No amounts on this page by rule. ✅ The unit itself is fine — the finding is about the counting, not the deal.
